title: Normalized scalar quotient presentation determines the coherent counit by double transpose
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ and an embedding $\iota:E\to L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. On $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $A_{E,m}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m)_W$, $B_m=(\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m)_W$ and $R_E=\varprojlim_mA_{E,m}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], with the same-index coefficient maps $A_{E,m}\to B_m$ and actual quotient transitions of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Let $S_Y$ be a normalized primitive scalar realization model for $\iota$ on $W$ in the sense of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], let $A$ be an object of the derived category of $R_E$-modules, and let $P\to A$ be a representative by a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R_E$-modules [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]. Let $C(P)$ be the strict $B_\bullet$-system with term $C(P)_m=(P\otimes_{R_E}A_{E,m})\otimes^L_{A_{E,m}}B_m$, let $a_m:C(P)_m\xrightarrow{\sim}P\otimes_{R_E}B_m$ be $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$, and use the actual quotient transitions. The canonical quotient presentation $(P,C(P),e_P,a)$ supplied by the normalized realization/effectivity data satisfies $\operatorname{CoefficientReductionPresentation}(P,C(P),e_P,a)$ of [def-pur-coefficient-reduction-presentation]. Let $u_{S_Y,P}$ be the scalar realization isomorphism and let $e_{C(P)}$ be the coherent reduction/realization counit. After identifying the target by the $a_m$, the composite $c_{S_Y,P}=e_{C(P)}\circ\mathcal R_L(u_{S_Y,P})$ is the unique coherent system morphism whose double transpose under the reduction/total-limit adjunction and the constant-tower/total-limit adjunction is the localization of the strict tensor-unit map determined by the $a_m$. The canonical coherent counit comparison $c^{\mathrm{can}}_P$ of [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] has the same double transpose; hence uniqueness of transposes gives $c_{S_Y,P}=c^{\mathrm{can}}_P$ as an entire coherent quotient-system morphism, with all actual transitions retained. This identifies the arbitrary normalized model comparison with the coefficient-extension model comparison before any finite-level evaluation.

proof.text: On the flat-term K-flat representative P, the finite-level scalar-association maps a_m are isomorphisms, and the actual quotient maps commute with them. The coherent counit/effectivity theorem for the normalized B-tower therefore supplies e_P and makes (P,C(P),e_P,a) satisfy both equations in CoefficientReductionPresentation: levelwise normalized reduction and every m≥n transition square. This is an assertion about the strict system, so all actual transitions are retained.

proof.text: The scalar-realization normalization of S_Y says that the reduction isomorphism u_{S_Y,P}, after the reduction/total-limit and constant-tower/total-limit adjunctions, transposes to the localization of the strict tensor-unit map determined by the a_m. By the adjunction R_L ⊣ L_L of the reduction calculus, the transpose of a map h into L_L C(P) is e_{C(P)}∘R_L(h); hence c_{S_Y,P}=e_{C(P)}∘R_L(u_{S_Y,P}) is exactly the reduction/total-limit transpose of u_{S_Y,P}, and by the unit/counit identities its inverse transpose L_L(c_{S_Y,P})∘η is u_{S_Y,P} again. So c_{S_Y,P} has the stated double transpose. The equality is in the whole derived system category, not merely after finite evaluation.

proof.text: Write D=(P⊗_{R_E}B_m)_m with its actual quotient transitions; by the definition of the integral scalar extension, S_{E,L}P is the total derived limit L_L D of this strict system, computed on P. The canonical comparison c^{can}_P of the coefficient-extension/reduction model is the coherent counit e_D:R_L L_L D→D followed by a^{-1}:D→C(P), the inverse of the scalar-association maps a_m. Naturality of the counit in the reduction calculus gives a^{-1}∘e_D=e_{C(P)}∘R_L L_L(a^{-1}), so c^{can}_P is the reduction/total-limit transpose of L_L(a^{-1}):L_L D→L_L C(P). Transposing L_L(a^{-1}) under constant-tower/total-limit gives the total-limit projection of D followed by the a_m^{-1}; on P this is x↦x⊗1∈P⊗B_m followed by a_m^{-1}, i.e. x↦(x⊗1)⊗1, and a_m((x⊗a)⊗b)=x⊗ab is the associator through which the two nested composites agree. Hence the double transpose of c^{can}_P is the same localized strict tensor-unit map determined by the a_m. The model's transition compatibility makes this an equality of entire coherent quotient-system morphisms.

proof.text: The composite of the reduction/total-limit transpose bijection and the constant-tower/total-limit transpose bijection is injective. Since c_{S_Y,P} and c^{can}_P have the same double transpose, uniqueness of transposes gives c_{S_Y,P}=c^{can}_P in the derived category of coherent quotient systems. An equality there implies equality of every evaluated component and of the induced transition squares, so the actual quotient transitions remain part of the conclusion.
